prompt: For $R\subseteq A\times A$, which condition defines antisymmetry? All quantified variables range over $A$.

answers.explanation: Mutual relatedness forces equality. Self-loops are allowed.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. This defines symmetry, not antisymmetry.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This defines reflexivity, not antisymmetry.
Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. This defines transitivity, not antisymmetry.
Every related pair has no reverse. Taking the two elements equal also forbids loops. This defines asymmetry, not antisymmetry.
No element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This defines irreflexivity, not antisymmetry.
Some related pair lacks its reverse; this is an existential violation. This defines failure of symmetry, not antisymmetry.
Every related pair is diagonal; some or all loops may be missing. This defines coreflexivity, not antisymmetry.
An element has at most one outgoing related element; it need not have any. This defines right-uniqueness, not antisymmetry.
All diagonal pairs and no off-diagonal pairs are present. This defines equality as the entire relation, not antisymmetry.
